value: Covered California (the state's official ACA marketplace)
detail: Shop and compare qualified health plans; the application also screens for Medi-Cal eligibility.

value: November 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027
detail: Enroll by December 31, 2026 for coverage starting January 1, 2027; January enrollments start February 1. Current members can renew or switch starting October 1, 2026.
source_name: Covered California - Federal Changes for Enrollers Quick Guide (June 19, 2026)
notes: Verified 2026-10-18: Covered California's guide states the June 12, 2026 ruling in City of Columbus v. Kennedy vacated the shortened annual open enrollment period for the 2027 plan year, reverting it to the normal three-month period of November 1 through January 31. CMS separately states the federally facilitated exchange window is November 1, 2026 - January 15, 2027. Enrollment dates are on Covered California's open-enrollment page.

value: Household income between 100% and 400% FPL
detail: In all states, income in this range qualifies for the premium tax credit that lowers monthly premiums; the credit is based on household information and estimated income entered on the application.
notes: For 2027 coverage, 400% FPL is $63,840 for one person using the 2026 guidelines ($15,960 x 4).

item: No work requirement on marketplace coverage
value: None
detail: Marketplace subsidies depend on income, household, and access to other coverage - the ACA premium tax credit rules contain no work-hours or community engagement test (unlike Medicaid's new requirement).
notes: Trading, rental, and interest income all count toward the MAGI used for PTC. Exception: a person who is Medi-Cal-eligible but denied/disenrolled for work-rule noncompliance cannot get Covered California financial help (see CC-13/WR-17).

value: Expired December 31, 2025
detail: The enhanced (ARPA/IRA) premium tax credits - which had eliminated the 400% FPL cliff and capped contributions - expired at the end of 2025; the One Big Beautiful Bill Act did not extend them, so permanent-law rules (100-400% FPL eligibility, subsidy cliff at 400%) apply to 2026 and 2027 coverage.

value: House passed a 3-year extension (H.R. 1834) on January 8, 2026 (230-196); the Senate has not passed it; not law as of the October 18, 2026 research snapshot
detail: The Senate rejected a three-year extension 51-48 on December 11, 2025 (60 votes needed); the House later passed H.R. 1834, which remains pending in the Senate.

value: Up to 200% FPL ($31,920 individual; $66,000 family of four)
detail: For 2027, California appropriated $300 million (up from $190 million) for the Covered California State Subsidy Program; more than 500,000 Californians are projected to receive a state subsidy in 2027 (about 30% of enrollees), and nearly 200,000 can choose from two Silver-tier plans with a $0 premium.

value: Silver 94 (100-150% FPL); Silver 87 (150-200% FPL); Silver 73 (200-250% FPL)
detail: Silver plan actuarial-value variants with reduced deductibles, copays, and out-of-pocket maximums for PTC-eligible households up to 250% FPL.

value: For tax years beginning after December 31, 2025, repayment caps are removed
detail: Section 71305 of P.L. 119-21 removed the limitation on repaying excess advance payments of the premium tax credit; starting with the 2026 tax year (filed in 2027), the full excess must be repaid if income was higher than estimated.
source_name: IRS - Repayment caps eliminated for excess APTC
notes: Report income changes to the Marketplace promptly to avoid a balance due.

value: At least $950 per adult and $475 per dependent child, or 2.5% of gross income over the filing threshold, whichever is higher
detail: California residents must have qualifying health coverage, claim an exemption, or pay the Individual Shared Responsibility Penalty with their state tax return; exemptions include income below the filing threshold, unaffordable coverage, a coverage gap of three months or less, and health care sharing ministry membership.
source_name: Franchise Tax Board - Personal Health Care Mandate

value: Preliminary weighted average increase of 9.9%
detail: Covered California announced a preliminary weighted average rate increase of 9.9% for the 2027 coverage year; final rates take effect January 1, 2027.

value: 2026 federal poverty guidelines
detail: For the 2027 plan year, subsidy thresholds are measured against the 2026 guidelines (e.g., 200% FPL = $31,920 for one person, per Covered California's July 2026 release).
notes: Verified 2026-10-18. Covered California's July 21, 2026 release states 2027 subsidy thresholds use the 2026 guidelines. The earlier note that healthcare.gov publishes updated 2027 income levels on November 1 could not be confirmed on healthcare.gov and has been removed - see FL-22 on the Flagged for Review page.

item: Subsidy bar after Medi-Cal work-rule loss
value: Full-cost plans only (no federal/state financial help) if Medi-Cal is lost for noncompliance
detail: DHCS tells members that losing Medi-Cal for not meeting the work/renewal rules means no financial help through Covered California and full-cost insurance instead; ACWDL 25-30 confirms people eligible for MAGI Medi-Cal who fail the work requirement are not eligible for subsidized Covered California coverage even if they meet all other Medi-Cal requirements. Buying an unsubsidized plan and reapplying for Medi-Cal remain possible.
source_name: DHCS MEDIL I26-25 member outreach letter (Sept 11, 2026)
notes: Does not affect people whose MAGI is above Medi-Cal limits in the first place.

item: Senate action on extending the enhanced credits (official roll call)
value: Cloture on the motion to proceed to S. 3385 rejected 51-48 on December 11, 2025; three-fifths (60) required
detail: U.S. Senate roll call vote 644, 119th Congress, 1st Session: 'On the Cloture Motion (Motion to Invoke Cloture: Motion to Proceed to S. 3385)', vote date December 11, 2025, 12:29 PM, required for majority 3/5, result 'Cloture Motion Rejected', YEAs 51, NAYs 48, Not Voting 1. S. 3385 is 'A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to extend the enhancement of the health care premium tax credit' (the Lower Health Care Costs Act), which CRS summarizes as extending the enhanced PTC for three years, through 2028.
notes: Re-sourced 2026-10-18 from a senator's press release to the official Senate roll-call record.

item: House action on extending the enhanced credits (official record)
value: H.R. 1834 passed the House 230-196 on January 8, 2026 (Roll no. 11); received in the Senate and placed on the Senate Legislative Calendar on February 10, 2026 (Calendar No. 319)
detail: Congress.gov record for H.R. 1834 (119th Congress): sponsor Rep. McGovern [D-MA-2], introduced March 4, 2025, official title 'To advance policy priorities that will break the gridlock', status 'Passed House', action 'Passed/agreed to in House: On passage Passed by the Yeas and Nays: 230 - 196 (Roll no. 11)', latest action 'Senate - 02/10/2026 Read the second time. Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 319.' Senator Cantwell's January 8, 2026 release describes the same 230-196 vote on a three-year extension of the ACA enhanced premium tax credits.
notes: The bill's official title does not describe its content - see flagged item FL-23. Not law as of the October 18, 2026 snapshot.

item: Federal open enrollment window for 2027 (federally facilitated exchange)
value: November 1, 2026 through January 15, 2027
detail: CMS statement dated July 31, 2026: 'Open Enrollment at the Federally-facilitated Exchange will begin on November 1, 2026, and end on January 15, 2027.' Covered California's own window is November 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027.
source_name: CMS - Statement regarding City of Columbus v. Kennedy (July 31, 2026)
notes: Different end dates apply to California's state-based exchange and the federal platform; do not confuse the two.

item: Cost-sharing reduction variants on Silver plans
value: Silver 94 (100-150% FPL); Silver 87 (150-200% FPL); Silver 73 (200-250% FPL); no reduction above 250% FPL
detail: CMS 2026 payment-parameters guidance, Table 1: 'Silver 94% AV CSR Plan Variant: Individuals eligible for CSRs under 45 CFR 155.305(g)(2)(i) (household income greater than or equal to 100 and less than or equal to 150 percent of FPL)'; 'Silver 87% AV... greater than 150 and less than or equal to 200 percent of FPL'; 'Silver 73% AV... greater than 200 and less than or equal to 250 percent of FPL.' For 2026 the reduced maximum annual limitation on cost sharing is $3,350 self-only / $6,700 other-than-self-only for the 94% and 87% variants and $8,100 / $16,200 for the 73% variant. For household incomes above 250% and up to 400% FPL CMS applies no reduction because the statutory reduction would push plan actuarial value above the 70% statutory level.
notes: The 2026 maximum annual limitation on cost sharing is $10,150 self-only / $20,300 other than self-only. American Indian/Alaska Native enrollees under 300% FPL are eligible for zero cost-sharing plan variants.

item: Repayment of excess advance premium tax credit
value: From tax year 2026 the full excess must be repaid; repayment caps no longer apply
detail: IRS: 'Beginning with tax year 2026, the taxpayer must repay the full amount of any excess advance payments of the premium tax credit (APTC). The repayment limits that previously capped how much taxpayers had to pay back no longer apply.' The 2027 federal payment-parameters final rule states: 'Section 71305 of the WFTC legislation eliminates, effective for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025, APTC repayment limits and requires individuals whose APTC exceeds their PTC to increase their tax liability by the amount of the excess.'
source_name: IRS - Repayment caps eliminated for excess APTC
notes: Attributed by the IRS to the Working Families Tax Cuts Act and by the Federal Register to section 71305 of the same law (P.L. 119-21) - see flagged item FL-20.

value: $950 per adult and $475 per dependent child (flat amount), or 2.5% of gross income over the filing threshold, whichever is higher
detail: FTB: 'The penalty will be the higher of either: A flat amount, based on the number of people in the tax household, or A percentage of the household income.' Flat amount: 'Pay $950 per adult and $475 per child.' Percentage: 'Pay 2.5% of the amount of gross income that exceeds the filing threshold requirements based on the tax filing status and number of dependents.' FTB's sample 2025 amounts: individual with income under $57,580 may pay $950; married couple under $115,146 may pay $1,900; family of four under $177,163 may pay $2,850.
source_name: Franchise Tax Board - Personal Health Care Mandate
notes: The $950/$475 figures are the amounts FTB labels for the 2025 tax year and are indexed; later-year amounts are not stated on the page - see flagged item FL-24.

item: California mandate exemptions claimable on the state return
value: Income below the filing threshold; unaffordable coverage; unaffordable family self-only coverage; coverage gap of three consecutive months or less; certain non-citizens not lawfully present; certain citizens living abroad; health care sharing ministry members; members of federally recognized tribes; incarceration; a household member born or adopted during the year; a household member who died; enrollment in limited or restricted-scope Medi-Cal
detail: FTB's 'Exemptions processed by FTB and Covered California' table lists these exemptions as claimable on the state income tax return. Covered California separately processes the religious conscience, affordability hardship, and general hardship exemptions.
source_name: Franchise Tax Board - Personal Health Care Mandate
notes: Exemptions processed by Covered California (religious conscience, affordability hardship, general hardship) are separate.

item: California state subsidy program - projected reach
value: More than 500,000 Californians projected to receive a state subsidy in 2027 (about 30% of enrollees); nearly 200,000 can choose two Silver-tier plans with a $0 premium
detail: Covered California's July 21, 2026 release: 'more than 500,000 Californians are projected to receive a state subsidy in 2027, about 30 percent of all enrollees. Additionally, nearly 200,000 can choose from two Silver-tier plans with a $0 premium.' It also estimates the program will open financial help to an additional 200,000 Californians who were not eligible in 2026 and prevent 90,000 people from dropping coverage in 2027.
